title: Batch Runner: validated jobs, dependencies and separate logs
description: Use the real threaded interface and file pickers to configure three channel-preserving conversions, check dependency order, save and reload the queue, then stop and continue real subprocess jobs.
objectives: Find Batch runner under Help and add module settings with explicit dependencies and overrides.
Observe an invalid dependency order, restore it and save the validated plan.
Reload the plan, stop between real jobs and continue without repeating completed work.
Inspect separate logs and independently verified pixels, channel identities and conversion records.
prerequisite: Use the three acquired four-channel fields from the tutorial test dataset and separate source and destination folders per job. The tutorial helper tools/tutorials/batch_data.py copies the originals byte-for-byte into explicit fov01_C1 through fov01_C4 TIFF names. Each converted example uses the demonstration coordinate A01; original plate/well coordinates are not reconstructed. The older recording incorrectly mapped its original filenames to four separate C01 fields, so it is not evidence of preserved channel metadata. This lesson executes only convert, not a full Mask-to-Classify chain. No model, AI request or biological finding is claimed. The queue has no dedicated Load test data, live image preview or plotting panel; use the Format Converter lesson for its Preview and Resume controls. Failure policies are shown but failing analyses, hard-crash recovery and GPU-driver isolation are not tested here.

scenes.narration: Open Help, then Batch runner. This shared menu tool combines headless module jobs, settings files, dependencies and separate logs. It runs its own jobs sequentially; that does not prevent another application or queue from using the same computer's resources.

Choose convert and use Choose settings to open the first JSON file. We prepared three real microscopy fields in separate folders, each with four explicitly named channel files. Their pixels are unchanged, but A zero one is a demonstration coordinate, not a recovered original well.

The settings specify source, destination and actual conversion, with preview and resume disabled. Add a descriptive label, then choose Add job. The first identifier is convert one. Validate the conversion and channel mapping on a small example before scheduling a larger batch.

For the second job, After names convert one. The override plate naming equals name changes its plate-name convention without rewriting the saved settings file. This dependency controls eligibility and order; it does not automatically make the second job consume the first job's output.

Add the third job with no dependency or override. All three use different output folders. The table shows their identifiers, labels, dependencies and pending state. Selecting a row loads its configuration into the editor; the displayed table is not an editable spreadsheet.

Move the second job above its prerequisite. Validation reports the later dependency and disables Run queue. The small problem pane may require scrolling to read the explanation and suggested fix. This verifies an actual refusal, not just a claim that the validator protects you.

Move it back below convert one, then move the independent third job above it. The valid order is now one, three, two. Choose Validate again: no problems remain. Ordering constraints are satisfied, but validation cannot establish whether an analysis answers your scientific question.

On failure offers continuation for independent jobs or stopping at the first failure. We inspected both and restored continuation. Stop after is three consecutive failures here; it counts failures, not proof that their causes are identical. This successful example does not exercise either failure outcome.

Use Save queue to preserve the ordered plan as JSON. We then removed the third job from this disposable in-memory queue and used Load queue to restore the saved three-job plan. The project folders were not deleted. Keep the settings files and inputs with that plan.

After Run queue starts the first real subprocess, press Stop. It finishes the active job before stopping: the first row says success and the other two say not run. This is not an immediate kill, and this controlled stop does not prove recovery from a computer crash.

Choose Run queue again. Only the two remaining jobs execute, in the saved order; the first job's timestamps stay unchanged. All three now show success. Separate subprocesses isolate ordinary job execution, but this demonstration does not guarantee protection against a system-wide GPU or memory failure.

Select each row to read its own log. Here the converter reports one well, one field and four channel identifiers, then four converted files and exit code zero. The name override appears in the second job's outputs. Logs provide evidence to inspect, not automatic proof of correct scientific results.

Across all three jobs, twelve output images matched every original pixel and the intended channel identities. Each conversion record also reports four attempts, four successes and no failures. Originals remain unchanged. For scripting, spacr.batch provides Job, Queue and run_queue; see the API lesson and the converter's dedicated preview tutorial.
